subject: DPA: transient logs retention scenarios and residency clarifications
messages:
From: Acme Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Hernandez <marta.hernandez@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Jul 2028 14:22:00 +0000
Subject: Questions on DPA: transient logs & residency

Hi Michael —

Thanks again for the DPA draft. Our security and procurement teams had a couple of specific follow-ups focused on short-lived telemetry and residency:

1) Transient/system logs: we need concrete language for how long request-level logs (request IDs, timestamps, IP hashes, KV cache metadata) are retained in non-prod and prod. Does Redwood offer a guaranteed maximum retention for ephemeral logs that we can put in the DPA?

2) Proof of deletion: when an erase is requested for a tenant, what evidence do you provide that transient logs were removed? Is a deletion manifest provided or is this limited to a confirmation note?

3) Residual backups and snapshots: do any snapshots/backups contain unredacted transient logs? If so, where are they stored (region), and what is the retention/erase flow?

We are trying to slot a redline back to Legal by next Tuesday. Any succinct options you can share (and the operational steps behind them) would be helpful.

Marta will be the internal lead on this — I’m CC’ing her.

Appreciate a short write-up we can attach to the DPA.

Best,
Acme Procurement
procurement@acmehealth.com

--
Attachment references: "current_dpa_draft.docx" (we did not receive a redline from Redwood yet)

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Acme Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marta Hernandez <marta.hernandez@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Jul 2028 09:08:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA: transient logs & residency

Marta / Acme team —

Thanks for the clear list. Below are three pragmatic options we present commonly; each maps to operational steps we can commit to in the DPA (and I attached a marked-up redline v2 for quick reference).

Option A — Tight ephemeral retention (default) - Description: Request-level/transient logs (request IDs, per-request telemetry, non-pii IP hashes) retained for max 30 days in prod; 14 days in non-prod. - Operational proof: We provide a deletion manifest showing truncated object IDs and timestamps plus an audit log entry of the erase job (job id, start/end, operator). - Snapshots: Snapshots exclude transient logs by default; nightly snapshot process prunes ephemeral buckets prior to artifact creation. - Tradeoffs: Lowest residual risk; slightly larger operational overhead for very short retention workloads.

Option B — Standard retention (balanced) - Description: 90-day retention for request-level logs in prod (30 days for non-prod). - Operational proof: Confirmation of erase job and retained-sample audit reports. For full forensic needs, retention windows are negotiable with a commercial uplift. - Snapshots: Backups are rolled daily; we can commit to an on-request targeted purge workflow for affected snapshots (documented SLAT).

Option C — Extended retention w/ regional carveout - Description: 1 year retention where customer requires longer forensic windows. - Operational proof: We provide deletion manifests and coordinate an ops-run to remove entries from active storage and initiate backup remediation (this may require accelerants for older snapshot indexes). - Snapshots: May require escrow or separate on-prem options to fully remove historical copies.

A few clarifying notes:
- "Transient logs" should be defined in the DPA as request-level telemetry (i.e., logs that are not part of user content or model outputs). We should avoid ambiguity with audit/security logs which often must be retained for compliance.
- For proof of deletion we typically provide manifest + ops-run audit entry. Where a customer requires signed evidence we can produce a signed deletion certificate (we list this as an add-on in our enterprise package).
- Region: We can ensure snapshots and backups are stored in the customer's chosen region (US: us-east-1 or us-west-2) and include a geo-lock clause to prevent cross-border replication.

If you want, I can loop in Jonas (legal/product) and Marissa (ops) with a suggested DPA paragraph and a short erase-playbook appendix. We can deliver a clean redline (DPA_redline_v3.docx) by EOD tomorrow if that timeline works.

Next step: are you comfortable with Option A or B as a starting point? If you pick A we will lock the 30-day language and include a deletion-manifest obligation.

Best,
Michael Grant
Senior Security Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference
michael_grant@redwood.com

Attachment: DPA_redline_v2.docx (marked for Acme review)

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Jul 2028 10:15:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Questions on DPA: transient logs & residency — proposed language

Jonas / Marissa — forwarding Acme procurement query and my proposed options (below). I drafted a short paragraph for the DPA and an operational appendix; please see my inline suggestions and the attached erase_playbook_v1.pdf. I want to keep commitments narrow and operationally verifiable.

Suggested DPA paragraph (draft):
"
"Transient logs" means request-level telemetry (request identifiers, timestamps, hashed IPs, KV cache metadata and diagnostic traces) that do not include customer data or model outputs. Redwood will retain transient logs for a maximum period defined per-environment (Prod: 30 days; Non-Prod: 14 days) unless the parties expressly agree in writing to a different retention period. Upon a valid erasure request, Redwood will: (i) execute the erase job against active storage; (ii) provide the customer with a deletion manifest containing object identifiers and timestamps for removed items; and (iii) record an audit entry showing the job id, operator id, and a hash of the manifest.
"

Operational appendix highlights (for internal ops runbook):
- Runbook step 3: prune ephemeral bucket before snapshot creation (cron: 01:15 UTC).
- Runbook step 7: manifest generation takes a maximum of 2 hours post-job completion.
- Runbook step 11: backup remediation request workflow (ticket -> scheduled remediation -> confirmation) — estimated SLA 10 business days for archives older than 90 days.

Jonas — can you confirm the liability/wording here is acceptable (the manifest + audit entry approach)? We want to avoid committing to cryptographically-signed certificates without an add-on. Marissa — confirm that the 2-hour manifest SLA and the 10 business days for archive remediation are operationally feasible.

Thanks,
Michael 

---
Jonas Weber (inline reply):
> Michael — the paragraph looks good. On the manifest: legal prefers we add a sentence limiting the scope to transient logs only and excluding any forensic items that are maintained for security reasons (e.g., intrusion detection). I will tweak that sentence and push back if they ask for signed deletion certificates as a standard term.

Marissa Cole (inline reply):
> 2-hour manifest SLA OK for standard volumes. For high-volume enterprise (multi-tenant bursts) we should surface an exception and propose a 24-hour manifest SLA unless they select the accelerated add-on. Also recommend we call out the region options explicitly (us-east-1/us-west-2) and a Geo-lock clause.

Attachments: erase_playbook_v1.pdf (ops appendix), internal_notes.txt

Subject: Re: Questions on DPA: transient logs & residency

Marta / Acme team —

Attached is our suggested redline (DPA_redline_v3.docx) and a short operational appendix (erase_playbook_v1.pdf) that explains the erase flow and evidence we can provide. Summary of the commitments we added:

- Defined "Transient logs" explicitly in the DPA to avoid overlap with security/audit logs.
- Committed to Option A by default (Prod 30 days, Non-Prod 14 days) — we can change to Option B per request.
- Evidence: deletion manifest + audit entry (job id/operator id/hash). Signed deletion certificates are available as an enterprise add-on; not a standard deliverable.
- Snapshots/backups: we will exclude transient log buckets prior to snapshot creation; for historical snapshot remediation we offer a documented on-request workflow with an SLA of 10 business days for archives older than 90 days (exceptions for deeply archived data noted in the appendix).
- Region: we will store backups in the customer-chosen US region and include a Geo-lock clause in the redline.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached redline and let us know if Option A is acceptable as the default.
2) If you want a shorter manifest SLA or signed deletion certificate as a standard part of the DPA, we can prepare an addendum and provide pricing.
3) If approved, we'll hand the redline to Legal and ops will prepare a dry-run of the erase-manifest flow for the account prior to signature.

Thanks — look forward to hearing which option you'd like to proceed with.

Best regards,
